Thanks Natalie — I’ve skimmed the redlines and highlighted the three areas below for legal/product input. Looping in Ben (contracts) and Laura (product/legal ops) to propose precise language. Quick asks for internal alignment before I reply to Vestra: 

1) Output ownership: Vestra’s exclusive-title ask is broader than our standard Order Form carveouts. We should offer a productization license limited to customer-generated outputs used in their internal applications, but not exclusive title for general model outputs.
2) Training/data use: agree to explicit opt-in for training and provide an SLA for data deletion and access controls; deny unfettered audit rights but offer a review process with redacted logs.
3) Feedback license: cannot be an unlimited cross-customer transfer — propose a revocable, non-exclusive improvements license limited to the improvements derived specifically from Vestra’s feedback and with attribution/timebound scope.

Ben — can you draft proposed redline snippets (MSA + Exhibit A) that accomplish the bullets above? Laura — can you confirm operational feasibility for the training opt-in + deletion SLA and the log-review workflow?

Kim / Laura — draft redline snippets below. I kept the language tight so legal can graft it into the MSA. Happy to iterate.

1) Output ownership (MSA, Section 3.2) — Proposed: 
"Customer retains ownership of Customer Content and any Outputs that are produced solely from Customer Content and Customer-provided prompts, provided that such Outputs are not derived from or combined with Redwood Confidential or third-party training data. Redwood shall have a non-exclusive, worldwide, perpetual right to use aggregated, de-identified Outputs for model operation and improvement subject to the Feedback License set forth below."

2) Training/Data Use (Order Form / Addendum) — Proposed: 
"Redwood will not include Customer Content in model training without Customer’s prior written consent (opt-in). Upon written request Redwood will provide a certificate of deletion for Customer Content that was used for ephemeral operational purposes. Audit requests for training artifacts will be handled through a mutually agreed review process; Redwood will provide redacted sampling and metadata, not raw training datasets or full model checkpoints."

3) Feedback License (MSA, New Section) — Proposed: 
"Customer grants Redwood a limited, royalty-free, revocable, non-exclusive license to use Feedback (as defined) to improve Redwood services. Such license does not grant Redwood the right to sell Customer Feedback to third parties or to use Customer Feedback to create customer-specific commercial models without Customer’s consent. The license terminates if Customer provides written revocation and Redwood will cease using new Feedback for model training within thirty (30) days of revocation."

Operational notes: 
- These keep Redwood’s ability to aggregate de-identified data for product improvement while limiting exclusive title claims.
- Keeps a 30 day revocation window to be operationally reasonable.

If that looks good I’ll formalize into tracked-change redlines against their PDF and return to Kimberly for review.

—Ben
Contracts Counsel, Redwood Inference

Hi Natalie / Vestra team — thanks for the redlines and the quick turnaround on procurement timing. Attached is a consolidated proposal from Redwood that addresses your three primary asks while preserving both parties’ operational needs. High-level summary: 

- Output ownership: We acknowledge customer ownership for Outputs generated solely from Customer Content and Customer prompts. We cannot concede exclusive title for model outputs more broadly; instead we propose a narrow productization license for customer-specific outputs to support productization and downstream commercial use by Vestra.
- Training/data use: We will only train models on Vestra content with explicit opt-in. We will provide deletion certificates and an agreed-upon, limited audit/review process (redacted sampling of logs and metadata) rather than full audit rights.
- Feedback license: We propose a limited, revocable, non-exclusive improvements license with a 30-day revocation window and an explicit prohibition on selling customer-specific Feedback to third parties.

Next steps: 
1) Please review the attached tracked-change redlines and confirm whether Vestra can accept the proposed productization license and the 30-day revocation on the feedback license.
2) If acceptable, Vestra Legal and Redwood can exchange a final Order Form for signature; we can route to DocuSign once both legal teams sign off.
3) Operational handoff: If you accept the deletion certificate + audit approach we’ll open a small infra ticket and schedule a 30-minute runbook sync with Laura to demonstrate the deletion evidence flow.

We aimed to keep this tight so procurement timelines hold — happy to jump on a short call tomorrow if useful.

Best regards,
Kimberly Park
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
